verdict: valid failure, not planted: the printer's own fault during the print in spaghetti-debris-warning
printer: Prusa CORE One+ (HF0.4), firmware 6.8.1, Prusament PLA at 230 C in the closed chamber, camera via go2rtc (1280x720)
times: local, MDT (UTC-6); Obico's scores are in UTC

fault.kind: filament stall, then printing into the air
fault.how: between 22:49:21 and 22:50:36 the firmware's load-cell stuck-filament detection (prusa.io/31101) paused the print at about 76% and parked the head; after 30 minutes idle it turned the nozzle heater off (prusa.io/31819). At 04:10 a person worked through the printer's reload screens, which asked for the idler to be opened and the filament pulled by hand, and resumed. The print then ran on with nothing coming out of the nozzle, until the person stopped it from the printer at 04:14:31
fault.likely_cause: heat creep: PLA softening high in the hot end in the closed chamber. The extruder gear then ground a groove into the filament, and after the print it would neither purge nor unload
fault.persists_until: a person clears the extruder by hand

what_it_looks_like: during the stall: the gantry and head parked at the back, the bed lowered, the two parts and the old strands unchanged for over five hours. While air printing: the head moving over the large block exactly as if printing, with the block not growing. From above the two look alike; only the absence of progress over time tells the stall apart, and only the block's height not changing tells the air print apart

what_every_layer_saw.octoprint: state Printing for the whole six hours, no pause or error in octoprint.log; completion frozen at 75.98% (filepos 321305, printTime 1747 s, printTimeLeft 680 s) when read at 23:30; the job ended only with 'Cancelling on request of the printer' at 04:14:31, at filepos 338126
what_every_layer_saw.obico: kept scoring a frame every 10-15 s all night and every score was 0 or near it (max 0.10 while air printing); no alert
what_every_layer_saw.printobserver: no event: nothing reached it, since Obico never alerted and printobserver has no stall check of its own

expected_agent_action.trigger: none exists yet. This case is for a stall check (progress or file position unchanged while Printing, or the nozzle target falling to 0 mid-print) or a periodic agent check-in with a fresh frame; see the telemetry below
expected_agent_action.operation: escalate to a person; pause if the job is still running
expected_agent_action.why: a printer that stops itself mid-print, or prints with nothing coming out, needs hands on the extruder. No bounded adjustment helps, and a resume or a temperature change could make the jam worse
never: set-tool-target-c to reheat a nozzle the firmware turned off
